# Attachments module: rules for AI edits

Read [MODULE.md](MODULE.md) first. The rules below are enforced by CI (`tools/build.ps1 -Target CI`); the Claude hooks refuse violating edits early. Owners: @platform-owner.

## Dependencies
- May depend on: `StarterDomain`, `StarterApplication`, `StarterInfrastructure`, `CodelabSecurity`, `CodelabErrors`
- Must not depend on: `Identity`, `Users`, `Access`, `Lookups`, `Audit`, `Settings`, `Jobs`, `Notifications`, `Portal`

## Required
- `base.thin-controllers`: Controllers and endpoints only bind input, call one Application use case and map the result; no business logic, no data access. (enforced by architecture-test, review, automated from P2)
- `base.application-ports-only`: Application code depends only on Domain types and ports (interfaces); it never references EF Core, DbContext or infrastructure types. (enforced by architecture-test, hook, automated from P1)
- `base.module-boundaries`: A module references another module only when listed in its mayDependOn, and never one listed in mustNotDependOn. (enforced by architecture-test, eslint, automated from P1)
- `base.endpoint-contract`: Every endpoint has a permission attribute, takes and returns PublicId (never raw database ids), validates its input with a validator and returns errors as problem+json. The text twins base.endpoint-has-permission and base.minimal-api-has-permission refuse an ungated endpoint early and name the new-endpoint skill. (enforced by contract-test, hook, review, automated from P2)
- `base.lookups-via-migrations`: Lookup and reference data is created and changed only through EF migrations, never by runtime seeders or manual SQL. The text twin base.lookup-seeded-by-migration refuses a seed outside a Migrations folder and names the new-lookup skill. (enforced by hook, review)
- `base.platform-owner-review`: Changes to rules/, packages/, .claude/, the exemptions of any module.rules.yaml, deploy/, .github/, docs/adr/, provenance/, tools/extract/, tools/build.ps1 and the repo-wide build settings need platform-owner review. (enforced by codeowners, hook)
- `base.enums-as-int`: Enums are stored and sent as integers and every enum member has an explicit numeric value (Approved = 3), so reordering never changes stored data; labels come from i18n, never from enum names. (enforced by hook, analyzer, automated from P1)
- `base.no-magic-values`: Status ids, role keys, permission keys, error codes, config keys, claim types, route names, cache keys, job ids and limits live in typed constants or options classes; numeric literals other than the allowed ones need a named constant. (enforced by hook, analyzer, eslint, automated from P1)
- `base.clean-code`: Use named arguments for non-obvious parameters, small single-purpose methods, guard clauses instead of nesting, meaningful names, and no dead or commented-out code; size and complexity stay within the module thresholds. (enforced by analyzer, review, automated from P1)
- `base.unit-tests-mandatory`: Every Application use case, validator, workflow transition, domain rule and Angular service or component with logic ships with unit tests, and each module meets its line-coverage threshold. (enforced by scaffold, commit-gate, review, automated from P2)
- `base.fe-ui-library`: Screens are built only from @codelab/ng-dga components and the 8 page patterns. (enforced by eslint, hook, review, automated from P2)
- `base.fe-no-raw-text`: No user-visible raw text in templates or components; every string is an i18n key present in both ar and en. (enforced by i18n-check, hook, automated from P2)
- `base.fe-tokens-logical-css`: Styles use design tokens (CSS variables) and logical properties (inline-start/end) so RTL and LTR both work. (enforced by stylelint, hook, automated from P2)
- `base.fe-permission-gated`: Every route and every action button is gated by a typed permission key (base.fe-routes-gated, base.fe-buttons-gated); the backend endpoint behind it carries [HasPermission] with the same key. Recipe docs/recipes/add-permission.md. (enforced by contract-test, scaffold, review, automated from P3)
- `base.fe-routes-gated`: Every route that renders a page (component or loadComponent) carries data.permission (RouteDataKeys.Permission, a generated PermissionKeys value) on itself or an ancestor, with permissionGuard() (tagged with Symbol.for('codelab.ng-tools.permission-guard'); an untagged guard fails as missing-guard) on itself or an ancestor, or its full path is in PUBLIC_ROUTE_PATHS (src/app/public-routes.ts); redirects are exempt and every lazily loaded child table is passed to the route-gates spec. Fix: add data: { [RouteDataKeys.Permission]: PermissionKeys.<Key> } or, for a page every visitor may open, the public path. Recipe docs/recipes/add-permission.md. (enforced by contract-test, review, automated from P3)
- `base.fe-buttons-gated`: Every action element (a <dga-button>; a <button> with any event binding, a submit button or a typeless one in a submitting form; a role=button element with an event binding; any element binding (click) or (confirm), such as a dialog host) in features/**/*.html and in the inline templates of features/**/*.ts carries *hasPermission="PermissionKeys.<Key>" (on itself, on an ancestor element, or [hasPermission] on an <ng-template> wrapper) or an explicit data-public-action for an action every visitor may take. Fix: add the directive with a generated key, or data-public-action. Recipe docs/recipes/add-permission.md. (enforced by contract-test, review, automated from P3)
- `attachments.thin-endpoints`: Every endpoint is a thin controller action in Api/ that calls one Application use case, carries [HasPermission] with an AttachmentsPermissionKeys constant and maps the Outcome with OutcomeResults; ids on the wire are PublicId<AttachmentIds> and PublicId<AttachableRecordIds>. (enforced by contract-test, review)
- `attachments.data-through-ports`: Application code reads and writes data only through ports it declares (IAttachmentStore, IAttachmentReceiptVerifier, IAttachmentStorageClient, IAttachmentFileCleanup, IUploadTicketIssuer); the implementations live in Infrastructure. (enforced by architecture-test, review)
- `attachments.record-access-gate`: Every use case that touches a record's attachments passes AttachableRecords.RefuseAsync (View for list and download, Change for ticket, link and remove) before reading or writing; a missing record and a denied one answer the same 404 (ATTACHMENTS_NOT_FOUND). (enforced by review)
- `attachments.receipt-only-metadata`: A link stores only what IAttachmentReceiptVerifier verified (file id, name, size, SHA-256; MIME type from the extension) after the receipt scope equals UploadScopes.For(record, type, user); never a client-sent hash, size or name. (enforced by review)
- `attachments.types-seeded-by-migrations`: Attachment types are never edited at run time except IsActive. The Attachments module seeds its own types by migration; a record type's types are declared by the module that owns the record type through Starter.Application.Attachments.IAttachmentTypeSeedSource and written at start by AttachmentTypeSynchronizer (AttachmentTypeSeeding.Plan, matched by key: insert missing, refresh names and rules, never change id, key, record type or IsActive). Every type uses an id from Starter.Domain.Attachments.AttachmentTypeIds and a key from AttachmentTypeKeys, never reused, and its extensions stay inside Codelab:Security:Uploads AllowedExtensions (checked at start). (enforced by review)
- `attachments.cleanup-after-save`: A removal is soft and saved first; the deletion of the bytes is enqueued afterwards through IAttachmentFileCleanup (outbox type attachments.delete-file), never called inline. (enforced by review)

## Forbidden
- `base.time-provider` (error) in `**/*.cs`: Reading the system clock directly makes time untestable. Fix: Inject TimeProvider and call GetUtcNow() (or GetLocalNow() for display); tests use FakeTimeProvider.
- `base.no-thread-sleep` (error) in `**/*.cs`: Thread.Sleep blocks a thread and makes waits untestable; it is also a global banned API (RS0030) in Codelab.Build.Sdk. Fix: Use await Task.Delay(delay, timeProvider, cancellationToken) so waits are async and testable.
- `base.no-scheduler-dashboard-mapping` (error) in `**/*.cs`: The Hangfire dashboard exposes enqueue, delete and requeue of every job behind its own authorization; the starter never maps it. Fix: Use the admin Jobs endpoints (jobs.view, jobs.run) and the log.
- `base.no-static-scheduler-storage` (error) in `**/*.cs`: Static Hangfire storage hides the database from DI and from tests; the storage comes from the JobStorage singleton of SchedulerRegistration. Fix: Resolve JobStorage from DI (SchedulerRegistration.AddJobScheduler registers it).
- `base.no-analyzer-opt-out` (error) in `**/*.cs`, `**/*.csproj`, `**/*.props`, `**/*.targets`, `**/.editorconfig`, `**/*.globalconfig`: Turning off the banned-API, complexity or clean-code (CLB) analyzers removes a build gate for everyone after you (a gate switch set to anything but true, the .NET analyzers or the analysis level off, by id, by a bare pragma, by category severity, by marking code generated, or by relaxing warnings-as-errors). Codelab.Build.Sdk also fails the build (CODELAB002, CODELAB003). Fix: Fix the code instead. A justified exception is a module.rules.yaml exemption with a reason, reviewed by the platform owner.
- `base.no-inline-suppression` (error) in `**/*.cs`, `**/*.csproj`, `**/*.props`, `**/*.targets`, `*/**/.editorconfig`, `**/*.globalconfig`: An inline suppression (a pragma, with or without a space after the '#'; the SuppressMessage attribute named anywhere, so an alias such as 'using SM = ...SuppressMessageAttribute' is caught too; a unicode escape outside a string or comment, which could spell that name; a NoWarn or WarningsNotAsErrors entry; WarningLevel 0; or a diagnostic severity set to none, silent or suggestion) switches an analyzer off without platform-owner review. Fix: Fix the code. A justified suppression is a module.rules.yaml `analyzers` severity (generated into the module .editorconfig) or an `exemptions` entry, both reviewed by the platform owner.
- `base.no-analyzer-config-redirect` (error) in `**/*.csproj`, `**/*.props`, `**/*.targets`: A CodeAnalysisRuleSet, GlobalAnalyzerConfigFiles, EditorConfigFiles, AdditionalFiles or Analyzer item in a project file points the analyzers at configuration (or a suppressor) that no platform owner reviewed, so it can switch any diagnostic off. Fix: Remove the item. Analyzer severities and thresholds come from the module.rules.yaml (generated into the module .editorconfig); a new analyzer or analyzer config is a platform-owner change to Codelab.Build.Sdk.
- `base.no-ruleset-file` (error) in `**/*.ruleset`: A .ruleset file can set any diagnostic to Action="None"; the starter configures analyzers only through the rules engine, so no ruleset may exist. Fix: Delete the file. Set analyzer severities in the module.rules.yaml, then run node tools/rules-engine/compile.mjs.
- `base.no-lint-suppression` (error) in `frontend/**/*.ts`, `frontend/**/*.html`, `frontend/**/*.scss`: An eslint, stylelint or TypeScript suppression comment (eslint-disable, an inline eslint config, stylelint-disable, @ts-ignore, @ts-nocheck) switches a frontend gate off without platform-owner review. Fix: Fix the code instead. A justified exception is a module.rules.yaml exemption with a reason, reviewed by the platform owner.
- `base.no-hand-written-editorconfig` (error) in `*/**/.editorconfig`: A nested .editorconfig applies to every file below it, so a hand-written one can switch analyzers off or change thresholds for part of a module; the only nested ones are those the rules engine emits at each module root. Fix: Delete the file. Set analyzer severities and thresholds in the module.rules.yaml, then run node tools/rules-engine/compile.mjs.
- `base.no-fixture-gate-opt-out` (error) in `**/*.cs`, `**/*.csproj`, `**/*.props`, `**/*.targets`, `**/*.rsp`, `**/*.ps1`, `**/*.mjs`, `**/*.json`: CodelabFixtureGateOptOut lets a build switch the quality gates off without CODELAB002; only the SDK's own fixture builds may pass it. Fix: Remove it. The quality gates stay on for every project; fix the code instead.
- `base.no-hand-written-globalconfig` (error) in `**/*.globalconfig`: Roslyn loads any .globalconfig it is given, at any global_level, so a hand-written one can raise the clean-code thresholds or switch rules off for a whole project; the only one is the generated rules/codelab.globalconfig. Fix: Delete the file. Change thresholds in rules/base.rules.yaml or a module.rules.yaml, then run node tools/rules-engine/compile.mjs.
- `base.no-auto-generated-marker` (error) in `**/*.cs`: An auto-generated header makes every analyzer skip the file (CLB1001-CLB1005 ignore generated code), so hand-written code must not carry one. Fix: Remove the header. Real generator output is written under obj/ by the build and is never committed.
- `base.no-generated-file-name` (error) in `**/*.g.cs`, `**/*.g.i.cs`, `**/*.generated.cs`, `**/*.designer.cs`, `**/*.Designer.cs`: A *.g.cs, *.generated.cs or *.designer.cs name makes the analyzers treat a hand-written file as generated and skip it. Fix: Rename the file to a plain *.cs name. Generator output lives under obj/ and is never committed.
- `base.no-test-project-opt-in` (error) in `**/*.csproj`, `**/*.props`, `**/*.targets`: Only a *.Tests project is a test project (CLB1004 magic numbers skips test projects). Production code may not declare IsTestProject, reference a test framework (Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk sets IsTestProject) or rename its assembly to *.Tests. Fix: Put tests in a project named <Module>.Tests; production code never declares IsTestProject.
- `base.no-accept-any-certificate` (error) in `**/*.cs`: A certificate validator that accepts everything turns TLS into plain text for an attacker in the path (the harvest source's internal calls did this). Fix: Keep certificate validation on. Trust an internal CA through Codelab.Integration's ServerCertificatePolicy (pinned or chain-validated), never by returning true.
- `base.no-threshold-override` (error) in `**/.editorconfig`, `**/*.globalconfig`: Clean-code thresholds (codelab_* keys) written by hand bypass the rules files and their review; only the files the rules engine emits, at their own paths (rules/codelab.globalconfig and each module's .editorconfig), may set them. A GENERATED marker in the content proves nothing. Fix: Change the thresholds or settings in rules/base.rules.yaml or the module.rules.yaml, then run node tools/rules-engine/compile.mjs.
- `base.no-string-permission-key` (error) in `**/*.cs`, `**/*.ts`: Permission keys passed as string literals drift from the permission catalog. Fix: Use the typed permission constant (Permissions.<Area>.<Action> in C#, PermissionKeys.<KEY> in TypeScript).
- `base.no-string-role-check` (error) in `**/*.cs`: Role checks with string literals bypass the permission model. Fix: Check a permission with [HasPermission(Permissions.<Area>.<Action>)] instead of a role name.
- `base.no-string-config-key` (error) in `**/*.cs`: Configuration read by string key is untyped and unvalidated. Fix: Bind a typed options class with a SectionName constant and ValidateOnStart, then inject IOptions<T>.
- `base.enum-stored-as-int` (error) in `**/*.cs`: Enums stored or serialized as strings break when a member is renamed. Fix: Keep the EF default (int column) and the numeric JSON value; the client maps numbers to i18n labels with the generated TS enum.
- `base.enum-explicit-values` (error) in `**/*.cs`: An enum member without an explicit value changes meaning when members are reordered (CLB1005 is the build gate). Fix: Give every enum member an explicit numeric value, e.g. Draft = 1, Submitted = 2.
- `base.no-dbcontext-in-api` (error) in `**/Api/**/*.cs`, `**/*.Api/**/*.cs`, `**/*Controller.cs`: The Api layer must not touch the database directly. Fix: Call an Application use case; only the composition root registers the DbContext.
- `base.no-ef-in-application` (error) in `**/Application/**/*.cs`, `**/*.Application/**/*.cs`: Application code must depend on ports, not on EF Core. Fix: Declare a port (repository or IUnitOfWork interface) in Application and implement it in Infrastructure.
- `base.public-id-routes` (error) in `**/*.cs`: Raw numeric or Guid database ids in routes leak internal keys. Fix: Take a PublicId route value ({id}) and resolve it in the Application layer.
- `base.endpoint-has-permission` (error) in `backend/src/**/*.cs`: A controller action without a permission attribute (or an allowlisted anonymous, authenticated or service gate) is open to every caller. Fix: Use the `new-endpoint` skill (node tools/scaffold/new-endpoint.mjs) to add the endpoint; it writes [HasPermission(<Module>PermissionKeys.<Key>)] with the permission, use case, validator and tests. An endpoint every visitor may call is [AllowAnonymous] plus a reviewed line in backend/tests/Starter.Contract.Tests/EndpointAllowlist.cs.
- `base.minimal-api-has-permission` (error) in `backend/src/**/*.cs`: A minimal-API mapping without a permission or an explicit anonymous or authenticated gate is open to every caller. Fix: Use the `new-endpoint` skill (node tools/scaffold/new-endpoint.mjs) for a controller action with [HasPermission]. A mapping that must stay minimal ends with .RequireAuthorization(...) or .AllowAnonymous() in the same statement, plus a reviewed line in backend/tests/Starter.Contract.Tests/EndpointAllowlist.cs.
- `base.transition-in-catalog` (error) in `backend/src/**/*.cs`: A transition rule or catalog built outside the record type's workflow class, or a status written directly, bypasses the transition catalog and its validation. Fix: Use the `new-transition` skill (node tools/scaffold/new-transition.mjs); it adds the status and the TransitionRule to Application/Workflow/<Entity>Workflow.cs with its wording, notification decision and tests. Status changes go through the workflow engine, never by assigning Status.
- `base.lookup-seeded-by-migration` (error) in `backend/src/**/*.cs`, `**/*.sql`: Lookup values seeded at run time, in model configuration or by hand-written SQL drift between environments and skip review. Fix: Use the `new-lookup` skill (node tools/scaffold/new-lookup.mjs); it writes the <Name>Ids constants, the LookupTypes key and the seed migration with Arabic and English names.
- `base.no-empty-catch` (error) in `**/*.cs`, `**/*.ts`: An empty catch block hides failures. Fix: Handle the error, or let it reach the global exception handler; log with the reference code when you rethrow.
- `base.no-commented-out-code` (warning) in `**/*.cs`, `**/*.ts`: Commented-out code is dead code; git keeps the history. Fix: Delete the commented-out code.
- `base.fe-http-via-api-service` (error) in `**/*.ts`: Feature code must not call HTTP directly. Fix: Inject ApiService (or the generated API client) from core/api; it owns the base URL, auth and signing headers.
- `base.fe-no-hardcoded-paths` (error) in `**/*.ts`: Route and API paths typed as literals drift from the route and API catalogs. Fix: Use the typed route constants (AppRoutes) and the generated API client instead of path literals.
- `base.fe-ui-library-only` (error) in `**/*.ts`: Third-party UI kits and external DGA packages are not allowed (D5). Fix: Use the matching component from @codelab/ng-dga, or ask the platform owner to add one.
- `base.fe-ui-library-styles-and-deps` (error) in `**/*.scss`, `**/*.css`, `**/package.json`, `**/angular.json`: Third-party UI kit stylesheets, dependencies (including npm aliases) and angular.json styles/scripts are not allowed (D5). Fix: Remove the UI kit's stylesheet, dependency (or its npm alias) or angular.json entry and use @codelab/ng-dga components and tokens, or ask the platform owner to add one.
- `base.fe-no-remote-stylesheet` (error) in `**/*.scss`, `**/*.css`: Stylesheets imported from a remote URL (CDN) are not allowed (D5, no egress). Fix: Install the stylesheet's package through the platform owner (or self-host the asset) and import it locally; UI kits stay refused (D5).
- `base.fe-shared-no-features` (error) in `**/src/app/shared/**/*.ts`, `**/src/app/patterns/**/*.ts`, `**/src/app/layouts/**/*.ts`: Shared building blocks (shared/, patterns/, layouts/) must not import feature code. Fix: Move what both need into shared/ (or core/), or pass it in through an input; a feature may import shared code, never the reverse.
- `base.fe-raw-text-in-template` (error) in `**/*.html`: Raw text in a template is not translated. Fix: Use the `new-screen` skill for screen work; add ar and en keys to the i18n files and use {{ 'feature.key' | translate }}.
- `base.fe-raw-text-in-inline-template` (error) in `**/*.ts`: Raw text in an inline component template is not translated. Fix: Use the `new-screen` skill for screen work; add ar and en keys to the i18n files and use {{ 'feature.key' | translate }} in the template.
- `base.fe-no-string-permission-key-in-template` (error) in `**/*.html`, `**/*.ts`: A permission key written as a string literal in a template gate drifts from the permission catalog (the template check refuses it too). Fix: Use the generated key, *hasPermission="PermissionKeys.<Key>" (docs/recipes/add-permission.md).
- `base.fe-logical-css` (error) in `**/*.scss`, `**/*.css`: Physical left/right properties break RTL. Fix: Use logical properties (margin-inline-start, inset-inline-end, text-align start/end).
- `base.fe-design-tokens` (error) in `**/*.scss`, `**/*.css`: Raw colours bypass the design tokens. Fix: Use a design token, e.g. var(--codelab-color-primary).
- `attachments.no-module-reference` (error) in `backend/src/Modules/Attachments/**/*.cs`, `backend/src/Modules/Attachments/**/*.csproj`: Record types plug in through the kernel port IAttachableRecordAccess; a reference to another module couples them and breaks removing one. Fix: Use a kernel port in Starter.Application (the owning module implements IAttachableRecordAccess and registers it).
- `attachments.no-file-bytes-in-database` (error) in `backend/src/Modules/Attachments/**/*.cs`: File bytes live only on the attachment service; a byte[] or base64 column in this module brings back the in-database attachments the starter left behind. Fix: Store the file on the attachment service and keep only its receipt-verified metadata in RecordAttachment.
- `attachments.no-has-data` (error) in `backend/src/Modules/Attachments/**/*.cs`: Attachment types are seeded by explicit migration InsertData calls, never by HasData in the model. Fix: Seed the type in a migration as docs/recipes/add-attachment-type.md shows.

Plus the global list in Codelab.Build.Sdk (DateTime.Now and friends, Thread.Sleep).
- _none_

- fileLines: 400
- cyclomaticComplexity: 10
- parameters: 5
- backendLineCoverage: 80
- frontendLineCoverage: 70
